text: wsl-claude: then two things make recall work. (1) FILING, which the clickable title now does going forward. Tonight's R19 talk is mostly in team/chat (about 250 lines from the three of us since 01:30), so for this plan the lead could post a short catch-up into transport/R19: the decisions only. (2) A 'DECIDED' block at the top of each requirement's dialog: the few rulings that shaped it, each with your words and when. Tonight's for R19: the log goes in node.db, backups carry the risk; the key is seq AUTOINCREMENT; hash and time are indexes, not keys; nothing above trafficLog.js changes; the move doesn't wait for R16. Recalling a requirement is then reading five lines, with the full thread below for anyone who wants the why.

CATCH-UP, decisions only, from tonight's team/chat (2026-09-28). DECIDED: (1) Goal, Andy's words: 'Moving the node log into machine-side database'. (2) Rule 1: nothing above trafficLog.js changes. Andy: 'that's a rule for this plan'. (3) Rule 2: the move doesn't wait for R16; proof columns come later, with warnings. Added by the lead without an explicit yes; Andy: 'it's a good rule, so we don't correct that behavior now'. (4) The log goes into node.db, and the risk is carried by backups. Andy: 'i'm ok with that risk, i'd rather rely on backups, and not worry about it'. (5) A backup comes first. Andy: 'it's required to pull this off safely and keep my node safer'. (6) Stale tests get updated. Andy: 'the related stale tests must be updated.' (7) The key is seq AUTOINCREMENT; hash and at are indexes, not keys. Andy: 'there will be a requirement naming the indexes required'. (8) Every row is kept: 'the log should be permanent. period.' stands. OPEN: where the backup goes (encrypted into Google Drive, or a folder that doesn't sync); R19.4 as three indexes (hash skipping blanks, at over owner rows, at over admitted arrivals); whether searches return seq; the restore epoch, deferred until seq leaves the node.

For it, as a proposal. Shape: while a goal is open and design mode is on, what you type in Team is filed under the goal's id, and Team shows that thread. Once you end design mode, Team files under team/chat again, so your next line starts a new design and clears the board, as now. For: nobody has to remember to click; the goal's thread fills by itself, and wsl's catch-up problem doesn't come back. Against: talk about one item typed in Team lands on the goal, not the item. That's still one click closer than team/chat, and the item's dialog is where item talk goes. Risk: design mode is detected from your Team lines today, so Desk must count lines under the goal as Team lines, or it would think design mode had ended. A small change, Desk only. Build it?

wsl-claude: yes, simpler: naming a goal makes the goal's thread the default, so the Team box posts under transport/R19 until the session ends, and nobody has to remember a filing rule (tonight shows we don't). One caveat: some things said during a session aren't about the goal (tonight: 'what's next', a Desk tweak, the backup's Google Drive question). Those would land under the goal too. That's harmless if the goal's dialog can mark a line 'not about this' and move it to team/chat later, or simply if we accept a little noise under the goal. I'd accept the noise; filing everything under the goal beats scattering it.
